claims.text: Pike Place & Pike Street had 141 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 0 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $9.7 million a year.
1% of crashes here were recorded as “pedalcyclist strikes pedalcyclist or pedestrian” crashes, against 0% at the city's worst crash locations.
1% of crashes here were recorded as “pedalcyclist struck pedestrian” crashes, against 0% at the city's worst crash locations.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -33% (95% interval -52% to -13%) at 371 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing); a second run of the same design on 366 sites agrees.

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 4.2 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $1.4 million a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

Lighting would avoid about 2.5 crashes a year (CMF 7774, the only eligible record; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $854,000 a year; check on site: the corner has no street lighting now.
The Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is responsible for 1st Avenue (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
